summary: This is not a bill — it explains what your plan paid for your specialist visit and lab work on June 9, 2026. Both services were covered in-network. The document shows a $50 copay (a fixed fee) for the specialist visit and $24 coinsurance (your percentage share) for the lab panel. No errors were found in the math on this EOB. Compare any bill from Bayview Endocrinology to these amounts before paying.

lines.explanation: You owe $50 for this specialist office visit. That is your plan's fixed specialist copay — PR-3 means "this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service" [CODE-PR-3], and your plan sets specialist copays at $50 [PLAN-COPAY]. Good news on the rest: the provider billed $260, but the plan's approved price was $145. The $115 difference is a CO-45 write-off (the discount your provider agreed to), and "Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care" [CODE-CO-45]. The plan paid $95.

citations.quote: PR-3 means this amount is a copay, a fixed dollar amount for a covered visit or service.
Office visit copays are $25 for primary care and $50 for specialists.
Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care.

lines.explanation: You owe $24 for this blood test (comprehensive metabolic panel). That is your coinsurance — your percentage share of the plan's allowed amount of $120, not of the $240 billed charge. PR-2 means "this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met" [CODE-PR-2]. The plan paid $96. The $120 gap between the billed charge and the approved price is a CO-45 write-off (the provider's agreed discount): "The difference is written off by the provider" [CODE-CO-45] — you never owe that part.

citations.quote: PR-2 means this amount is coinsurance, your percentage share of the allowed amount after the deductible is met.
The difference is written off by the provider. Members do not owe CO-45 amounts for in-network care.

actions: Keep this EOB and wait for the bill from Bayview Endocrinology Associates before paying anything — an EOB is not a bill.
When the provider's bill arrives, verify it matches this EOB: $50 for the June 9 office visit (CPT 99214) and $24 for the lab panel (CPT 80053), and nothing more.

If the bill asks for more than these amounts — especially any part of the write-off amounts ($115 or $120) — call the billing office and point to this EOB, since those are provider write-offs you do not owe.
